## How they got there
Inter reached the final as a runner-up after losing to Paris Saint-Germain 0-5, having advanced through the knockout stages where they ranked seventh by probability. The model identified that their path was most supported by stats where they beat more teams than any other metric in this group: 78% on passes per game and 60% on shots per game, alongside a 50% advantage in long passes.

## Would the model have picked them?
With a 12.9% probability of reaching the final compared to an 8.3% base rate, Inter ranked seventh among all knockout teams, meaning the model did not pick them as it only selects from the top two ranks for finalists. Their expected stage figure of 0.87 places them nearest to the quarter-finals on the scale, indicating a statistical association with exiting before the semi-final despite beating the base rate probability.

## Weak spots
The team's weakest areas were shot accuracy at 39.2%, where they beat only 8% of that season's teams, and distance covered per game at 68.1 km, where they beat just 3%. Although the model marked down fouls committed per game with a negative contribution, Inter actually ranked highly by beating 83% of their peers on this stat. The model also penalized attacks per game, yet this was not among their absolute lowest rankings in the full dataset.

messages.content: You are a football performance analyst writing for a curious, data-literate reader. Use ONLY the facts provided. Quote every number exactly as it appears in the facts, with the same rounding. Do not introduce players, managers, matches, events, analyses or numbers that are not in the facts. 'Better than this %' figures say how many teams the club beat on a stat, so higher is always better, including for stats marked '(lower is better)', where beating a team means having the lower value. SHAP contributions are measured in knockout stages: a positive contribution means the stat pushed the model's expected stage up by that fraction of a round, a negative one pushed it down. A SHAP contribution is the model's view, not a measure of how good the team was at the stat: a team can rank high on a stat the model marked down, so never call a stat a strength or a weakness because of its SHAP sign. Everything here is a statistical association, not a cause: never say a stat drove, propelled, hindered or prevented a result, and do not explain why a stat got its contribution. Write plain markdown without tables.
